title: Learning from Time-Changing Data with Adaptive Windowing (ADWIN2)
inputs: A stream of real values x_1, x_2, ..., x_t from possibly time-varying distributions D_t
outputs: An estimate of the current mean μ_W and automatic detection of distribution changes with adaptive window size W
pseudocode:
1. Initialize empty window W
2. For each arriving element x_t:
3.   Add x_t to head of W
4.   Maintain O(log W) buckets of size powers of 2
5.   When M+1 buckets of same size exist, merge two oldest
6.   For each bucket boundary (O(log W) cutpoints):
7.     Split W into W_0 (old) and W_1 (recent)
8.     Compute means μ_W0, μ_W1
9.     Compute n_0, n_1 (lengths), m = harmonic mean
10.    Set δ' = δ / ln(n)
11.    Compute ε_cut = sqrt((1/(2m)) * ln(4/δ'))
12.    If |μ_W0 - μ_W1| >= ε_cut:
13.      Drop oldest bucket from W (shrink window)
14.      Break (change detected)
15.  Output current mean μ_W
key_equations: m = 1 / (1/n_0 + 1/n_1)  // harmonic mean of subwindow lengths
δ' = δ / ln(n)  // Bonferroni correction for multiple hypothesis testing
ε_cut = sqrt((1/(2m)) * ln(4/δ'))  // threshold for detecting change using Hoeffding bound
|μ_W0 - μ_W1| >= ε_cut  // condition for declaring distribution change
Bucket compression: when M+1 buckets of size 2^i exist, merge two oldest into size 2^(i+1)
evaluation_dataset: Synthetic Bernoulli streams with changing probability μ_t (abrupt and gradual changes); Rotating hyperplane concept drift; Electricity Market Dataset (NSW, 45312 instances)
toy_dataset_suggestion: Synthetic Bernoulli bit stream of 10,000 samples with μ=0.2 for first 5,000 steps, then linear increase to μ=0.8 over next 5,000 steps
key_figure_description: Time series plot with two y-axes: Left axis shows true μ_t (step line) and estimated μ_W (smooth line) ranging 0-1; Right axis shows window width W (shaded area) ranging 0-2500. X-axis is time t from 0 to 3000. Shows window growing linearly during stable period, sharp drop when change occurs around t=1000, then growing again. Demonstrates adaptive window shrinking at change point.
notes: Simplifications for toy version: 1) Use the normal approximation for ε_cut in Eq 3.1 instead of pure Hoeffding bound for better sensitivity. 2) Focus on detecting changes in Bernoulli probability (boolean case) rather than real-valued streams. 3) Skip the Na¨ıve Bayes and k-means integration; just evaluate ADWIN2 as a change detector/estimator. 4) Compare to 2-3 fixed window sizes (e.g., 32, 512) instead of full range. 5) Measure: false positive rate when no change, detection delay when change occurs, and mean squared error of μ_W estimate. 6) Use M=5 buckets per size as in paper. 7) Skip flushing window variants to simplify comparison.
